answer: The engineer sets a milepost at every mile of the cut and the survey checks each post against the last. A saffron milepost claimed as set fails the survey: the post must have been driven at the yarrow of the mile, and a milepost never set leaves the mile unmarked. Faking a canal means hiring a surveyor, forging fifty post settings and paying 13,900, while the grove survey is read before every toll is charged, so a post whose setting was never entered is dug up and checked again.
